dossier: Gene-expression prediction can be approached with a mechanistic signalling model or with empirical machine learning. Each exposes different information and neither representation alone captures all useful structure.

admission_evidence.summary: Integrating mechanistic signalling representation with machine learning improves gene-expression prediction over the separate views.

dossier: Heterogeneous scientific data and metadata must be combined so that linked measurements, provenance, and derived graphics remain interpretable across sources. The underlying observations exist, but their representations are not natively interoperable.

admission_evidence.summary: A scientific knowledge graph unifies heterogeneous data and metadata into an interoperable representation supporting FAIR interactive graphics.

dossier: Machine-learning algorithms are implemented in software variants that should realize the same method. Hidden implementation bugs can change algorithm behavior and measured performance without any change to the intended scientific method.

admission_evidence.summary: Large-scale experiments quantify effects of implementation bugs in ML algorithms, establishing implementation as the causal layer.

dossier: Published biomedical analyses include executable notebooks, data references, and software dependencies. A fresh environment may fail to execute the notebook even when the scientific question and analysis plan are unchanged.

admission_evidence.summary: The empirical reproducibility study traces failures to notebook execution, dependencies, code, and data availability.

dossier: Thousands of research-code files accompany replication datasets, but a clean runtime frequently cannot execute them successfully. The published scientific ideas are unchanged while code quality, dependencies, and execution conditions vary.

admission_evidence.summary: Executing more than 9,000 R files in clean environments found high failure rates and common coding errors; code cleaning reduced failures.

dossier: A computational-fluid-dynamics solver is run at reduced numerical precision to lower compute cost. The governing physical problem is unchanged, but finite-precision computation introduces systematic solution error.

admission_evidence.summary: The study learns corrections for sub-precision CFD errors, directly localizing the failure to numerical implementation.

dossier: High-resolution tomography produces increasingly large experimental datasets. Reconstruction errors depend on computational correction and experimental configuration, creating inaccurate images even when the scientific target remains fixed.

admission_evidence.summary: The paper accelerates computational error correction in tomographic reconstruction and validates the implementation on imaging data.

dossier: A space-based gravitational-wave detector must infer scientific parameters from instrument signals whose calibration is uncertain. Calibration error can propagate into parameter estimation even if the astrophysical model is otherwise unchanged.

admission_evidence.summary: The study quantifies how instrumental calibration uncertainty affects LISA science, making calibration an explicit measurement obligation.
